correctness.rationale: Exact finite polynomial derivatives imply terminal law. Explicit polynomial numerator P_n has one coefficient sign change and opposite signs at zero and one; Descartes and intermediate value theorem force the unique strict minimum for all n>=3. Positive abundance partitions with at most three individuals are all flat or monotone decreasing; (1,3) supplies sharp four-person realization. Exact coefficient and endpoint tests plus root trials support but do not replace proof.

value.rationale: Terminal sign is a complete, directly abundance-frequency interpretable mathematical boundary for the instantaneous species-area exponent in every fixed-census model; the only-relevant singleton and doubleton classes are ecologically natural rarity groups. The one-singleton/one-common-species subclass has a complete global all-integer turning classification and sharp minimal census, a natural exact structural cutoff rather than an arbitrary finite computation. No empirical claims or unsupported generalization are made.
